questions.question: Describe the basic statistical techniques used by journalists to analyse data.
questions.solution_html:
• Descriptive Statistics: Descriptive statistics summarise and describe the main
  • characteristics of a dataset. They help journalists present large amounts of
  • information in a simple and understandable form.
  • Percentages and Proportions: Percentages express a value as a part of 100. They
  • allow journalists to explain the relative size of a group or the share of a particular
  • category within a total.
  • Ratios and Rates: Ratios compare two quantities, while rates measure how
  • frequently something occurs in relation to a population, period, or other specified
  • unit.
  • Frequency Distribution: Frequency distribution shows how often particular values or
  • categories appear in a dataset. It organises information into categories, making
  • patterns easier to identify.
  • Data comparison – Trend Analysis – Correlation – Sampling and Survey Analysis –
  • Percentage Change – Cross Tabulation – Data Visualization

questions.question: How can a journalist extract useful information from a PDF report?
questions.solution_html:
• Useful information can be extracted from a PDF report through PDF scraping. PDF
  • scraping is the process of extracting text, tables, images, or other useful information
  • from a PDF (Portable Document Format) file for analysis or further use. This process
  • may include the following steps: Identify the PDf, extract the data, clean the data,
  • organize the data and analyze the data.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How would you use web scraping to collect information from multiple web pages?
questions.solution_html:
• Web scraping is the process of automatically collecting information from multiple
  • web pages using software or scripts. To handle multiple web pages in this process,
  • one should follow the following steps: Identify the websites, inspect the web pages,
  • choose a scraping tool, extract data, handle multiple web pages (use loops,
  • pagination or links to navigate through multiple pages), clean and organize the data,
  • and verify the data.

questions.question: How can a journalist identify misleading patterns in a dataset?
questions.solution_html:
• A journalist can identify misleading patterns in a dataset by carefully examining the
  • data, checking its accuracy, and looking for distortions or inconsistencies. One can
  • follow the following steps to ensure the same: check the data source, look for
  • missing data, identify outliers, check for bias, verify statistical claims, compare with
  • other sources, examine visualization techniques, and distinguish correlation from
  • causation.

questions.question: Discuss the major concepts of Data Journalism and explain how they enhance the accuracy and credibility of a news story.
questions.solution_html:
• Data journalism is the practice of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting
  • data to discover and communicate news stories.
  • Major concepts:
  • Data Collection: Gathering information from sources such as government reports,
  • surveys, websites, public records, and databases.
  • Data Cleaning: Removing errors, duplicates, and inconsistencies to improve the
  • quality of data.
  • Data Analysis: Examining data to identify patterns, trends, relationships, and
  • significant findings.
  • Data Visualization: Presenting information through charts, graphs, maps, and info
  • graphics to make complex data easier to understand.
  • Data Scraping: Automatically collecting information from websites or extracting data
  • from documents such as PDFs.
  • Statistical Analysis: Using statistical methods, such as averages, percentages, and
  • comparisons, to interpret data accurately.
  • Storytelling with Data: Using data-driven findings to develop meaningful news stories
  • that explain important issues.
  • Verification and Fact-Checking: Checking the accuracy, reliability, and credibility of
  • data before publishing a story.
  • Ethics and Transparency: Protecting privacy, avoiding bias, and explaining data
  • sources and methods honestly.
  • Interactive Journalism: Using interactive maps, charts, and dashboards to allow
  • readers to explore data themselves.
  • Accuracy and credibility are two important qualities required for data journalism.
  • Credibility can be ensured by double checking and verifying the collected data via
  • multiple reliable sources. Accuracy can ensured through data filtering, data cleaning,
  • and data organization.

questions.question: Evaluate the importance of simplifying complex data without changing its original meaning.
questions.solution_html:
• Simplifying complex data is an important part of data journalism because it helps
  • readers understand complicated information easily while preserving its accuracy and
  • original meaning.
  • The major effects of data simplification are as follows: Improves understanding –
  • Increases accessibility – supports better storytelling – maintains accuracy – Prevents -
  • misleading information – Saves time – builds public trust
  • Simplifying complex data makes news more accessible, meaningful, and engaging.
  • However, clarity should never come at the cost of accuracy. Journalists must simplify
  • the presentation without distorting the original meaning or hiding important
  • information.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of data journalism in investigating social issues such as poverty, unemployment, education, crime and public health. [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Data journalism is the practice of collecting, analyzing, and presenting data to
  • investigate issues and communicate news stories. It plays an important role in
  • uncovering social problems, exposing inequalities, and holding governments and
  • institutions accountable.
  • Poverty: Data journalism helps identify poverty levels, income inequality, and
  • differences in living standards across regions. Journalists analyze census data,
  • household surveys, and government reports to reveal which communities lack basic
  • necessities.
  • Unemployment: It helps investigate unemployment rates, job opportunities, wage
  • differences, and employment trends. By comparing data across age groups, genders,
  • and regions, journalists can identify groups most affected by unemployment.
  • Education: Data journalism examines literacy rates, school dropout rates, student
  • performance, teacher shortages, and access to educational facilities. It can reveal
  • inequalities between rural and urban schools and between different social groups.
  • Crime: Journalists use crime statistics to identify crime trends, high-risk areas, and
  • changes in reported offences. Comparing police records with other sources can help
  • investigate public safety issues. However, differences in reporting practices must be
  • considered.
  • Public health: Data journalism analyzes disease rates, hospital facilities, vaccination
  • coverage, mortality rates, and access to healthcare. It helps reveal gaps in healthcare
  • services and evaluate the effectiveness of public health programmes.
  • By examining public records, budgets, and official statistics, journalists can identify
  • misuse of public funds, ineffective policies, and failures in public services. This
  • encourages transparency and better governance.
  • Charts, graphs, maps, and interactive visualizations make complex social problems
  • easier to understand. They help readers recognize the scale of an issue and make
  • informed decisions.
  • [15x2=30]
